fields.why: Fall and fall-injury percentages are compared across 3 age groups (with p<0.01 for increase), race groups, and are tabulated across income and education levels.
Age (3 ordered groups), race (4+ groups named in claims) and SES (6 income and 4 education levels in Table 1) qualify; sex is 2 groups, and marital and health status are not SPDs.

'Increased with age (p<0.01)' with orthogonal polynomial contrasts is a trend test; race claims under the blanket 'pairwise t-tests' are per-group vs referent only; income and education are only shown in Table 1 with no reported test result, so side by side despite the methods line listing them among compared subgroups (the flag does not change this).

brief_issues: A methods line that lists an SPD among the subgroups compared with named tests, but reports no result for it, is not covered; the brief's 'a methods line ... with no claim resting on it' wording for CI overlap suggests side by side, and saying so for named tests generally would close it.
